title: 8086: BIU, EU, segments and assembly
subtitle: A 16-bit processor that fetches the next instruction while executing the current one — and reaches 1 MB with 16-bit registers.

split.title: BIU and EU
split.body: The 8086 is split into a Bus Interface Unit (BIU) that generates addresses, fetches instructions into a 6-byte queue and reads/writes memory, and an Execution Unit (EU) that decodes and executes from the queue. While the EU works on one instruction the BIU is already fetching the next: a two-stage pipeline. A jump empties the queue.

regs.title: Registers
regs.body: General registers AX, BX, CX, DX (each splits into high/low bytes AH/AL…), pointers SP, BP, and index registers SI, DI; segment registers CS, DS, SS, ES; instruction pointer IP; and a flag register with carry, parity, auxiliary carry, zero, sign, overflow and the control flags trap, interrupt, direction. CX often counts loops; BX is a base address; DX holds I/O ports.

seg.title: Segmented memory: a 20-bit address from 16-bit registers
seg.body: 16-bit registers reach only 64 KB, yet the 8086 addresses 1 MB. Every address is a segment:offset pair; the physical address is segment × 16 + offset (shift the segment left 4 bits and add). Code is fetched from CS:IP, data from DS:offset, the stack from SS:SP. Many pairs name the same byte: 2000:0010 and 2001:0000 are both 20010H.
seg.steps: Segment 2000H, offset 0050H. Physical = 2000H × 10H + 0050H. The same byte as 2005H:0000H, since 2005H × 10H = 20050H.

modes.title: Addressing modes
modes.body: Register (MOV AX,BX); immediate (MOV AX,1234H); direct (MOV AX,[2000H]); register indirect (MOV AX,[BX]); based (MOV AX,[BX+4]); indexed (MOV AX,[SI]); based-indexed (MOV AX,[BX+SI+8]). Memory operands default to the DS segment, except those using BP, which default to SS.

asm.title: Assembly language, assembling and linking
asm.body: An assembly statement has label, mnemonic, operands and a comment. Directives (SEGMENT, DB, DW, ASSUME, END) guide the assembler but emit no instructions. The tool chain: editor → assembler (.ASM → .OBJ; a two-pass assembler builds the symbol table on pass 1 and emits code on pass 2) → linker (.OBJ → .EXE) → run. DOS services through INT 21H (AH = 09H prints a string, 4CH terminates) and INT 10H (video).

prog.title: A first 8086 program, traced with the 8085 engine
prog.body: The same patterns — pointer, counter, loop, compare — apply on the 8086 with different mnemonics: MOV CX,4, ADD AL,[SI], INC SI, LOOP AGAIN (decrements CX and jumps if non-zero). Practise the ideas on the simulator with the 8085 equivalent.
prog.steps: 8086 version of the same loop. MOV CX,3 / MOV SI,2050H / XOR AL,AL / AGAIN: ADD AL,[SI] / INC SI / LOOP AGAIN.
